newsitem.title: GERMANY: Unworried by Buba, Bunds seen stuck in ranges.
newsitem.headline: Unworried by Buba, Bunds seen stuck in ranges.

text.p: Bund futures looked set to spend yet another day drifting in now familiar ranges on Thursday, unworried by even the prospect of a Bundesbank statement on the revaluation of official reserves.
Traders said at least until U.S. economic data at 1230 GMT, and probably thereafter, the DTB Bund future will remain between 100.50 and 101.00 -- a range that has persisted much of the week.
At 0737 GMT, the DTB Bund future was up six basis points at 100.81 after having traded in an early range between 100.70 and 100.83.
The major focus during European trading should be the Bundesbank council meeting where Bonn's plans to revalue German official reserves is to be discussed.
Six out of 10 analysts surveyed by Reuters on Tuesday said they expected the Bundesbank to approve the plan.
"I don't see a big impact. The revaluation plan has already been talked about a great deal," said Hans Nordstrom, trader at BMP Wertpapiere und Optionen GmbH.
There is no word yet from the Bundesbank on if it will make a statement on the scheme.

Indeed, maybe more important for the Bund market will be U.S. retail sales and jobless claims data due at 1230 GMT. Both figures could be important for Treasuries which could have a big impact on Bunds.
U.S. debt, however, has been outperforming Bunds of late, a trend which some expect to continue.
MCM YieldWatch said it expected the spread to move toward 85 basis points in coming days as EMU nerves increase ahead of the Amsterdam summit next week.
The spread stood at 89 basis points early this morning.

Traders also said they saw little market-moving news from the Franco-German summit in France on Friday, saying they expected Bonn and Paris to reach a compromise on the stability pact and that a public fight was unlikely.
The benchmark cash Bund was unchanged in early trade at 101.49 with the yield at 5.79 percent.
The yield curve likewise was little changed with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities at 233 basis points.
"Its a bit of a summer market," Nordstrom said. "Its hard to see what will excite the market."
